prompt: How do you decide which freshness horizon applies to which read?
chosen: Each read declares its own expiry: room sync = the presence watcher's 10-min cadence; usage-watch = the 50-min rule; money-item re-verify = verified-data hold until something could plausibly move it. Freshness is a property of the artifact (its cadence, its volatility, its last check), never of the run's anxiety. Log the horizon read-back - what was inherited and when it expires - so the next run can decide on facts, not feelings.
rejected: Use one global freshness rule for everything, or better: trust gut instinct - if something feels important, re-check it regardless of the last check. Horizon-per-artifact is over-engineering.

meta.episode: 2026-10-22 ella-pm-head run 298: per-artifact horizons, not global anxiety

prompt: The 00:47 presence sync's horizon lapses mid-run at 00:57 and the run is still working at 00:58. What then?
chosen: Then it lapses, and only then do I re-probe - elapsed time is what ends a horizon, not suspicion. A lapsed horizon is a new fact: the room state is now genuinely unknown, and one fresh sync is the honest move. The discipline is symmetric: don't probe inside the horizon, do probe when it dies.
rejected: Since it lapses soon, probe now anyway - the horizon is going to expire, so early re-probing is just being ahead of the schedule. Expiry boundaries are approximate.

meta.episode: 2026-10-22 ella-pm-head run 298: horizon death = the only trigger for re-probing

prompt: Nothing moved on the board for six overnight runs and the horizons say everything is still fresh. Did any of those runs do anything real?
chosen: Yes - each one did its one real leftover step (a verified Phase 0 batch) and logged honestly that the board was unchanged inside its horizons. Horizon discipline does not forbid work; it forbids re-reading the same fresh facts to look busy. The leftover step is chosen because it is verifiable, not because it is visible.
rejected: No - six quiet runs with no visible movement means the lane is drifting. If the horizons keep saying 'fresh', loosen them so the runs have something to do. Busyness is how you prove the lane is alive.
